history.note: React #419 fixed: identity.ts guarded localStorage for the static render; _layout.tsx mounts the route tree after hydration via useIsHydrated(). Verified zero page/console errors on menu, match-lobby, replay-library (classic) and match-dealt (3d); full legacy Playwright suite 103 passed / 1 skipped.

Placeholder triangle overrun closed by the real table (83,522 tris, 11 draw calls). Lighthouse regression from the menu backdrop fixed (0.66 → green) by deferring the mount past idle and skipping it on the low tier.

issues.title: Portrait: ~140 CSS px near-black band between the near rail and the hand; the 'floor-shadow ellipse' is imperceptible
issues.detail: Round-2 issue #5 was moved, not solved. The far rail is now pinned 55 px under the seat strip (good, toasts sit on the rail), but the near rail's bottom edge lands at y~550 CSS and the hand's top row starts at y~690, so the slack became a 140 px dead band. Pixel samples across it are rgb(14,21,17) centre vs rgb(15-16,22-24,17-20) at the edges — the ellipse is below perceptual threshold, so it reads as void, not shadow (crop p-dealt-band.png). The engineer calls it structural, but it is the default phone view of the whole product. Fix options: (a) treat the band as a persistent action tray rather than void — move the hand block up to rail-bottom + 28 px, and park the turn-status pill, the ClaimBar slot and the footer (badge + sort) in the recovered ~110 px at the bottom so the space is always occupied by HUD; or (b) scale the portrait fit from x ±11.65 to ~±10.6 (the racks sit at ~±10.2 so they stay in frame) which grows the table ~10% and halves the band, and make the shadow real: warm-black ellipse, peak alpha >= 0.35, ~60% viewport width, centred 20 px under the rail.

issues.title: Landscape opening-rolls modal overlaps the hand row; scene veil is desktop-only
issues.state: match-dice @ phone-landscape 915x412 (3d); compare match-dice @ desktop and phone
issues.detail: The glass 'OPENING ROLLS' panel spans y~97-318 CSS while the hand tiles' tops are at y~300, so the modal's bottom edge and gold border cut across the top ~17 px of every hand tile (六..發). Every landscape match opens with this, and it is the same overlap that made the tutorial's landscape ring bisect the hand (tutorial issue #1, table-owned half). Also inconsistent: on desktop the whole scene is dimmed behind the modal (tiles go grey), on phone and landscape there is no veil at all. Fix: a landscape size variant — 56 px dice, 8 px paddings, 11 px name labels, single row — capped at ~180 px tall and anchored so bottom <= hand top - 12 px; apply the same 0.45 veil on every viewport (or none).

issues.title: Desktop lobby: the waiting table is cropped by the right viewport edge while the glass column has a 110 px empty left margin
issues.detail: The backdrop finally exists (good), but the composition is unbalanced: the far wall runs from behind the Seats panel to a corner at x~1230, the right wall exits the frame at x=1440/y~450 and the near wall (blue tops, y 570-660) runs straight off the right edge with no rail — the table looks like it is sliding out of the screen. Meanwhile x 0-110 is void beside the glass column. Fix: recentre the desktop lobby camera so the right rail is >= 24 px inside the viewport (plate at ~x 1050, the centre of the free column), and pull the glass column to a 48 px inset or centre the two as a pair; landscape phone already frames it acceptably.

issues.title: Side-seat melds are wedged between the side wall and the rack; glyphs sideways at ~18 CSS px
issues.state: match-mid-hand, match-claim @ phone (南 meld, x~362-385 CSS); match-claim @ desktop (Jin's meld, x 1045-1090); match-claim @ phone-landscape (x~1320-1380)
issues.detail: With a full 18-stack side wall, the meld tiles laid in the rack line have their inner edge within ~2 CSS px of the wall's projected top edge, so they read as jammed against (or tucked under) the wall (crops p-midhand-rightmeld.png, d-claim-rightmeld.png). The far/near seats have room; only the side seats suffer. Fix: when the wall on that side is >= 12 stacks, offset side-seat melds 0.6 world units outward (behind the rack line toward the rail) or scale side-seat melds 1.1x; alternatively place melds at the near end of the rack (toward the camera) where the wall has usually been drawn down.

issues.title: River zoom: a ~5 px sliver of far-wall tile tops still peeks under the seat strip
issues.detail: Round-2 #3 is mostly fixed — the chrome row + seat strip now read as one dark panel from y=0 — but at x~272-390 CSS a row of five ivory tile edges shows for ~5 px directly under the strip (crop p-zoom-topright.png). Push the zoom anchor a further 8 px or extend the header glass 8 px below the seat strip so the wall's projected top is fully covered.

issues.title: Landscape footer ClaimBar touches the hand's bottom edge (0-2 px)
issues.detail: The new 41 px footer strip is the right solution and no longer sits on the wall, but its top border coincides with the hand tiles' bottom edge (crop l-claim-footer.png), so the tiles look like they stand on the panel. Reserve a 6 px gap in the landscape camera solve during a claim window (hand bottom >= strip top - 6) or trim the strip to 38 px. The engineer's disclosed two-row wrap case (three-option chi + PASS + long name) would grow into the hand — cap the strip to one row by hiding preview tiles when width > 480.

issues.title: Portrait full-table river glyphs are ~20 CSS px — crisper at dpr 2 but 索 still guess-level
issues.detail: The renderer now runs dpr 2 on phone (perf JSON), which sharpened the atlas; 六七八萬 and 中/東 are readable, but bamboo/dots faces at ~20 px, and the upside-down far river, are still identified by colour pattern rather than read (crop p-midhand-river.png). Zoom remains the path; a 1.1x river tile scale in portrait only would tip these to readable without touching the budget.

issues.title: Dead-wall marker: the ivory-tan back variant is unambiguous but reads as a different tile set
issues.detail: Round-2 #6 is closed — no kink, no misaligned stacks, the dead wall is instantly identifiable. Design note only: seven strongly tan stacks against sky-blue live stacks look like mixed tile sets rather than a marked segment. Consider a subtler blend (mix 0.6 toward the tan) plus a 2 px gold hairline on the felt under the dead segment, or keep it as-is if the clarity is preferred.

history.notes: 4 rounds: 7.9 → 8.2 → 8.2 → 8.3. Zero errors; 11 draw calls / 83k triangles / 9 programs on every state. Merged into integration; open issues carried forward.

issues.title: Desktop: a drift tile back sits on the hero rack's 一萬 corner (rack keep-out is phone-only)
issues.detail: At (277-330, 195-235) CSS a blue tile back overlaps the top-left corner of the rack's first tile 一萬 (crop c-desk-rack-left.png: the back's lower edge lands on the tile's bevel). The report says the projected-silhouette rack+dice keep-out was added 'on phones'; desktop and landscape still let the field touch the hero. It is a moving-field frame, but the seed is deterministic so every first paint shows it. Fix: apply the same projected rack silhouette + dice keep-out (2 px ramp) on every viewport, not only when width < tablet; assert in three-menu.spec desktop case that no drift disc intersects the rack rect.

issues.title: Desktop replay shelf reads small and aliased inside a 620 px card
issues.detail: Tiles are ~46 CSS px wide; the seven-tile illustration spans x 550-905 (57 % of the card's inner width) with 28 px of air above and ~100 px of shadow + air before the 'Nothing on the shelf yet' heading (crop c-desk-shelf-wide.png). At dpr 1 the silhouettes and 東南西 strokes show stair-steps (SwiftShader ignores MSAA). Phone (dpr 2) looks right — tiles 60 CSS px, clean edges. Fix: on desktop size the shelf canvas to ~72 % of the card's inner width (tile ≈ 58 px) and trim the pad below the shadow to ~0.25 tile widths; render at min(2, dpr*2) when dpr < 1.5, the same supersampling path the settings preview uses.

issues.title: Reduced-motion portrait field is one lone edge-on tile in the left margin
issues.detail: With animations off the frozen field shows a single tile seen edge-on at (8-28, 262-298) CSS beside the rack (crop c-phone-rm-tile.png). It is whole and clear of the rack, but one dark sliver in the margin reads as a stray speck, not a field. Either park all of them (rack + dice alone is cleaner, as landscape RM shows) or seed 2-3 whole, face-up tiles in the band between the rack bottom (306) and the Online card (341) / the footer strip. Known gap carried from round 1 (#5), still low.

issues.title: DISMISS pill label is ~0.55-alpha grey, below the 0.62 secondary-text spec
issues.detail: Sampled glyph pixels are #8c908e on #0d1310 → 6.0:1, so it clears 4.5:1, but rgba(255,255,255,0.62) over that glass would be ≈#a2a5a3. Use the shared secondary token so the pill matches EDIT / micro-labels. Persists from round-1 issue #11.

issues.title: Settings landscape letterbox still leaves ~38 % of the preview canvas as void
issues.detail: The rail spans x 280-635 of a 570-wide canvas (62 %); tiles are ~50 CSS px tall, legible but modest, with 65-70 px of dark void each side. HFOV 60 is fine; instead let PREVIEW_MAX_ASPECT rise to ~2.4 or grow previewHeight to ~170-180 by trimming the section gap so the stage fills the frame. Settings issue #7 from round 1, partially improved.

issues.title: Desktop dpr 1 preview: stair-step edges on tiles and glyph strokes
issues.detail: Crop c-desk-preview.png shows jaggies on the tile silhouettes and 五/萬/發 strokes at 3x. SwiftShader-only or not, the preview is 5-7 draw calls / 42k tris so a 2x supersample when dpr < 1.5 is cheap. Settings issue #3, unchanged; verify on a real GPU before deciding.

issues.title: Regression run hijacked by a stale serve on 4173 (process hazard, not a menu defect)
issues.state: npx playwright test three-menu/three-settings/... from the menu worktree
issues.detail: The first run reported 11 failures (debug.dice not iterable, replay-shelf-3d not attached, void rgb(125,95,78) under the LIVE PREVIEW pill) because playwright.config's reuseExistingServer: !CI reused a `serve dist -l 4173` started at 04:22 from /home/user/mm-wt/table — a different worktree's bundle. Re-running with a wrapper config on port 4991 serving this worktree's dist gave 18 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed. Suggest the e2e script pick a free port (PW_PORT env) or the runbook kill stale 4173 servers before `pnpm e2e`; the engineer's 'green' claim was only verifiable after that.

history.notes: Round-2 polish pass (menu + settings preview) passed at iteration 2 (8.1 → 8.6): drift/dice keep-outs, 3D replay shelf, settings preview framing/badge/hover/labels. Merged into integration.

issues.title: Phone portrait: rail corners clip the frame edge and the Live preview pill sits on the wood
issues.detail: In shots/critic-r2-phone/settings.phone.classic.png the near rail's rounded corners run into the preview frame's left and right edges (x~30 and x~795 of the 824px capture) so there is no void either side at the widest point, and only ~14 CSS px of void beneath the near bevel; the 'LIVE PREVIEW' badge (left 12, bottom 10) therefore overlaps the wood rail rather than floating in the parlour void as it does on desktop and phone-landscape. Fix: for aspects below ~1.9 back the camera off slightly (e.g. PREVIEW_CAMERA.position z 6.35 -> ~6.9, or PREVIEW_HFOV_DEG 52 -> ~56 in previewConfig.ts) so ~8-10 px of void separates the rail from the frame on all four sides, and/or move the badge to the top-left where the void is guaranteed. The three-settings spec's 'void below' assertion should then sample 8 px up with margin to spare.

issues.title: Blue back still reads cyan/pale toward the far edge
issues.detail: Measured centre of the face-down tile is #6b9db4 (phone) / #669ab3 (desktop): ΔE 3.5-3.7 against the Blue gradient, which is fine, but the far (top) edge is ΔE 5.5 (phone) and 6.8 (desktop) from the #7fa9c1 top stop and visibly cooler/more cyan than the chip. Plum behaves the same (far edge ΔE 9-10 vs top stop, 4 vs gradient). The single global albedo x0.8 / chroma x1.4 in compensateBackColor over-saturates cool hues. Fix: compensate per hue (e.g. saturation 1.25 for blue/mint, 1.4 for plum) or raise uBackRoughness toward 0.85 so the key's specular lift on the far edge drops; re-measure both edges, not just the centre.

issues.title: Desktop dpr 1 preview shows stair-step aliasing on tile edges and glyph strokes
issues.detail: At 3x zoom of shots/critic-r2-desktop/settings-jade-plum.desktop.classic.png the tile silhouettes and the 五/萬/發 strokes have visible jaggies; antialias:true is requested in SceneHost but SwiftShader does not honour MSAA, and the canvas is only 403x236 CSS px. Because the preview is tiny (6.6k tris, 5 draw calls) it can afford supersampling: render at min(2, dpr*2) via the new maxDpr path when dpr < 1.5, or add an FXAA/SMAA pass on desktop only. Verify on a real GPU before deciding whether this is SwiftShader-only.

issues.title: No hover state on skin chips or segmented controls
issues.detail: The visual language specifies hover = translateY(-1px) + brightness(1.05) over 160 ms for buttons; SkinChip and Segmented in SettingsPanel.tsx only style the pressed state (scale 0.97, surfaceHi). On a pointer device the chips feel inert until clicked. Fix: use Pressable's onHoverIn/onHoverOut (react-native-web supports them) to set a hovered style with the 1 px lift and a brightness filter, with a 160 ms transition.

issues.title: Status pill and Live preview badge use 10 px labels (spec is 11 px)
issues.detail: StatusPill text ('CLASSIC ACTIVE') is fontSize 10 with letterSpacing 1.2 and the 'LIVE PREVIEW' badge is fontSize 10 / letterSpacing 2; the shared language says small labels are 11 px, uppercase, 2 px tracking, weight 700. Contrast is fine (0.62 white over glass ~7:1) but 10 px at dpr 1 is at the edge of comfortable. Bump both to 11 px and align the pill's tracking to 2 px.

issues.title: match-dealt (table-owned) exceeds the triangle budget: 159,938 > 150,000
issues.detail: Zero errors on all three viewports, but budget.violations lists 'triangles 159938 > 150000' on each; the number is byte-identical to round 1 (critic-r1-phone-3d) and comes from the placeholder Table3DShell (3 draw calls, renders 1). Not attributable to the settings subsystem, so it is not counted against perfPass here — the orchestrator should keep gating it on the table subsystem. The warmupMs split (236-676 ms) and the gl.finish() change did remove the multi-second frame-2 stall seen in r1 (p95 2.2 -> steady-state 0 with renders 1).

issues.title: Phone landscape stage is small with ~45% of the canvas as empty void
issues.detail: The 570x150 letterbox keeps both rails in frame (void luminance 0.006 above / 0.009 below, verified), but the rail occupies only ~55% of the width and the tiles are ~40 CSS px tall — legible but modest. Options: let PREVIEW_MAX_ASPECT rise to ~2.4 so the stage uses more width while still keeping void above/below, or grow previewHeight to ~170 px at height < 520 by trimming the section gap (22 -> 16) in the landscape layout.

history.notes: Passed round 2 (8.4 → 8.6). Merged into integration at e5bc1f3.

issues.title: 3D landscape own-hand ring runs through the footer badge and the SUIT sort pill
issues.detail: The hand tiles end at y~365 CSS but the halo's bottom stroke sits at y~376 (HALO_PAD + overhang), while the footer chrome — 'Sharp Carp 東 莊' badge (x 12-165) and the SUIT/NUMBER/MANUAL pill (x 705-905) — starts at y~370. Crop shots/crops/ls-b2-footer.png shows the 1.5 px gold line crossing the avatar and the top of the SUIT pill, and the pill reads half-lit inside the hole. The spec's 'never bisect' rule is about tiles, but a gold ring slicing HUD controls is the same visual defect. Fix: when the footer chrome rect is within ~12 px of the target's bottom, clamp the halo bottom to that rect's top and treat the side as tight (drop the stroke and feather it, as the strip/hand case already does), or register the footer badge + sort pill as avoid rects so trimStraddlers cuts the ring back. Pin with a landscape case in placement.test.ts.

issues.title: Green dragon 發 ink is 3.8-3.9:1 on the spotlit hand (and unlit); landscape red 萬 sits right at 4.5
issues.detail: Per-tile probe: 發 core-median green (84,116,78) on face (230,218,190) = 3.80:1 at phone, 5.9 only for its black outline; at landscape the red 萬 darkest pixel (158,56,42) is 4.54:1 with most glyph pixels blended lower because the mark is ~14 px tall. Black numerals 9.9-13.2:1 and suit greens 5.7-6.4:1 clear comfortably, so the spotlight fix is sound — this is atlas ink. Fix: darken the 發 atlas green from ~#54744e toward ~#2f6a3a (target >= 4.5:1 on #e6dabe) and deepen the red 萬 ink one step (~#9e2a1e) so the small landscape mark keeps >= 4.5 after mip blending; re-run the per-tile probe.

issues.title: Scroll-cue chevron is painted over the last visible line instead of in the fade gutter
issues.state: tutorial-scoring-0 @ phone-landscape (3d and classic); tutorial-scoring-1 / match-result side dock @ phone-landscape (classic)
issues.detail: The 24 px fade + chevron is the right cue, but the chevron's tip lands on the text itself — over 'common' in 'six common scoring rules' (crop ls-s0-chevron.png) and over 'lowest' in 'The cleanest, lowest-faan' (cls-ls-s1-chevron.png). It reads as a glyph collision rather than an affordance. Fix: reserve ~14 px below the capped body for the chevron (bodyMaxHeight -= 14 when capped) and centre it in that gutter beneath the gradient, so the third line stays whole and the chevron sits on glass.

issues.title: Compact side dock says 'STEP 5/6' while every other card says 'STEP n OF m'
issues.detail: The narrow (<260 px) side-docked card switches the header to the 'STEP 5/6' form (TutorialOverlay.tsx ~line 890), so a user who sees 'STEP 1 OF 6' … 'STEP 3 OF 6' then 'STEP 5/6' within one lesson gets two label grammars. Fix: keep 'STEP n OF m' and let the stacked header wrap, or use the slash form everywhere. Related: the same 3D landscape card is only ~167 CSS px wide (title wraps to two lines, eight body lines) although the dimmed right wall stack beside the ring is not chrome — let side docks cover non-chrome scene geometry so the card can take >= 240 px.

issues.title: Desktop river ring clips the dealer chip's edge; chip inclusion differs per viewport
issues.state: tutorial-basics-4 @ desktop 1440x900 (3d); compare phone and phone-landscape
issues.detail: Crop desk-b4-chip.png: the 莊 chip spans x 913-965 and the ring's right stroke sits at x~962, so the gold line crosses the chip's right rim by ~3 px. At phone the chip is fully inside the hole, at landscape fully outside (dimmed) — three different treatments of the same object. Fix: either include the dealer-chip pocket in the published river interior rect at every viewport (it is part of the pool's frame) or subtract its projected rect so the ring never lands on it; pick one and pin it in targets.test.ts.

issues.title: Card settles 6 px after measurement during the entrance
issues.state: tutorial-basics-0 @ desktop (3d), observed under x1/x4/x8 CPU throttle
issues.detail: The throttled probe saw the CTA rect move from y 518 to y 512 (estimate-placed card refined by the measured height) while the opacity entrance was still running — a small visible hop of the whole card at the moment the user's eye lands on it. Fix: derive CARD_HEIGHT_ESTIMATE from the step's line count (title lines + wrapped body lines at the card width) so the estimate matches the measurement for standard cards, or animate the refine with the same 220 ms ease instead of snapping.

issues.title: Classic desktop scoring-1 ring top crosses the 北/南 seat badges (round-1 #3 residual)
issues.detail: Crop cls-desk-s1-top.png: the halo's top stroke at y~245 passes through the lower halves of the 'Jin 北' and 'Dao 南' badges (y 222-265), which are dimmed but still bisected by the gold line. Landscape classic is now clean (seat strip sits above the ring). Classic shells were out of scope this round; noting it so the scoreboard stays honest. Fix: exclude seat-badge rects from straddler enclosure or start the halo at the result panel's own top edge (HALO_PAD 8) on the desktop classic layout.

issues.title: Portrait: 140 CSS px near-black void between the near rail and the hand on the default phone view
issues.detail: Centre-column luminance scan of match-dealt.phone: rail wood ends at y~550 CSS (rgb 48,20,6), then y 575-690 samples rgb(10-15,14-24,10-19) (lum 13-22) until the hand's top row at y~700. issues.title: Landscape opening-rolls modal sits on the hand tile tops, and landscape gets no scene veil

issues.detail: The glass panel spans y~107-302 CSS and the hand tiles' tops start at y~300, so the panel's bottom edge and gold hairline cut the top of every hand tile 六..發 (crop wg2-crops/l-dice-handtop.png). Every landscape hand starts like this. Veil inconsistency measured: mean image luminance match-dealt vs match-dice is 70.8 -> 43.5 on phone and 61.3 -> 34.2 on desktop, but 44.4 -> 44.3 on landscape - identical, so the landscape scene is not dimmed behind the modal while the other two viewports are. Fix: a landscape size variant (56 px dice, 8 px paddings, 11 px name labels, single row) capped at ~180 px tall and anchored so bottom <= hand top - 12 px; apply the same 0.45 veil on every viewport.

issues.title: Desktop pre-game lobby: the waiting table slides off the right edge while 110 px of void sits left of the glass column
issues.detail: Crop wg2-crops/d-lobby-table.png: far wall runs from behind the Seats panel to a corner at x~1230, the right wall exits the frame at x=1440, the near wall (blue tops, y 570-660) runs straight off the right edge with no rail visible, and x 0-110 is empty beside the glass column. The backdrop exists (good) but the composition reads as a table half out of shot. Phone-landscape already frames it acceptably (rail visible right of the Rules panel). issues.title: tutorial-claims-0 shows a half-dollied table: hand clipped at desktop, touching the footer on phone, entirely off-screen on landscape
issues.state: tutorial-claims-0 @ desktop 1440x900, phone 412x915, phone-landscape 915x412 (3d) - reproduced deterministically in shots/wg2-extra
issues.detail: Compared with every other table state the whole scene is shifted down and ~10% larger: far seat badge first-light row at y=192 vs 168 (basics-1) / 162 (match-dealt); desktop hand bottoms at y~890 against the 900 px edge (crop wg2-crops/d-claims0-footer.png); phone second hand row ends at y~860 CSS, flush with the badge/sort footer (p-claims0-footer.png); landscape shows only the tile tops at y~395-412 - the hand the card tells you to discard from is not visible (l-claims0-footer.png). Perf JSON shows renders=3 in 1200 ms, and the camera rig eases with an exponential spring (halfLife 0.22 s, dt capped 0.5 s per rendered frame), so this is most likely the intro camera move caught mid-flight under SwiftShader - the recipe is the only tutorial state that neither waits for the own hand nor for a modal. On a 60 fps device the ease settles in ~1.2 s. Actions: (a) make the recipe waitForOwnHand + settle like tutorial-scoring-0 so the evidence is honest; (b) product hardening: gate the coach card's entrance on rig.update() returning false (camera settled), or snap the camera when intro travel exceeds a threshold, so lesson step 1 never appears over a half-dollied table on slow devices; (c) confirm on a real GPU before closing.

issues.detail: Crop wg2-crops/l-midhand-footer.png: the strip is the right solution (on the rail, not the wall) but its top border coincides with the hand tiles' bottom edge so the tiles look like they stand on the panel. issues.title: Coach-card glass is transparent enough for scene geometry to read through the header
issues.detail: Crop wg2-crops/p-dg2-cardheader.png: a river tile (dots face) shows through the card between 'LESSON 11/14' and the step dots, sitting on the header row like a stray glyph; in basics-1 the far wall's stacks show through the body copy. Fix: raise the card fill to ~0.86 alpha (or add a 12 px backdrop blur where supported) so the veil-dimmed scene becomes texture, not shapes; keep the 0.62 secondary text token.

issues.title: Portrait full-table river glyphs (~20 CSS px) are pattern-recognised, not read
issues.detail: dpr 2 sharpened the atlas (六七八萬, 中, 東 read) but bamboo/dots faces and the upside-down far river are still identified by colour pattern; the river-zoom view is the real fix and works. A 1.1x river tile scale in portrait only would tip these to readable without touching the budget.

issues.title: River zoom: a ~5 px sliver of far-wall tile tops peeks under the seat strip
issues.detail: Crop wg2-crops/p-zoom-sliver.png: five ivory tile edges show for ~5 px directly under the strip at x~272-390 CSS. Push the zoom anchor 8 px further or extend the header glass 8 px below the strip.

issues.title: Dead-wall tan segment reads as a second tile set rather than a marked segment
issues.detail: Seven strongly tan stacks against sky-blue live stacks are instantly identifiable (the round-1 kink is gone) but look like mixed sets. Consider mixing 0.6 toward the tan plus a 2 px gold hairline on the felt under the dead segment, or keep as-is if clarity is preferred - design note only.

issues.title: Landscape chrome residuals: DISMISS pill contrast, side-dock 'STEP 5/6' grammar, tile-sheet capture with the dice modal undismissed
issues.state: menu, replay-library, settings @ phone-landscape (DISMISS); tutorial-basics-4 @ phone-landscape (side dock); tile-sheet @ phone-landscape
issues.detail: DISMISS label is still ~0.55-alpha grey (#8c908e on #0d1310, 6.0:1 - passes AA but below the 0.62 secondary token used by EDIT and the micro-labels). The narrow (~167 px) side-docked card in basics-4 switches to 'STEP 5/6' while every other card says 'STEP n OF m', and its title wraps to two lines - let side docks cover non-chrome scene geometry so the card can take >= 240 px. The landscape tile-sheet capture shows the OPENING ROLLS modal still up over the debug sheet (phone and desktop tile-sheet are clean) - the dismiss tap did not land in landscape; check the recipe's dismiss hit target / the modal's tap-anywhere surface under that aspect.

issues.title: Settings/replay residuals: Blue back reads pale toward the far edge, dpr-1 stair-steps, phone replay page gap
issues.state: settings @ phone + desktop; settings, settings-jade-plum, replay-library @ desktop (dpr 1); replay-library @ phone
issues.detail: The face-down Blue tile in the preview is visibly cooler/paler at its far edge than the Blue chip (compensateBackColor's global chroma x1.4 over-saturates cool hues - compensate per hue or raise back roughness to ~0.85). On desktop at dpr 1 the preview tiles/glyph strokes and the replay shelf show stair-stepped edges (SwiftShader ignores MSAA; supersample 2x when dpr < 1.5 - both scenes are 5-7 draw calls so it is cheap). On phone the replay library leaves ~280 CSS px of void between the Auto-record card and the shelf card (crop wg2-crops/p-replay-gap.png) - pull the shelf card up under the toggle or centre the pair vertically.

verdicts.why: B's perspective table with plum tile backs, wooden rim, and large two-row hand reads as a real game scene with depth; A is a flat green panel that is mostly empty space with small hand tiles. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill and bot-skill labels are clearer, and B wastes a large dark band above the table.

A has depth, a readable large hand, dealer chip and dice detail, and a clear DISCARD status pill; B is a flat dark-green layout dominated by an empty discards box. B's compact top bar shows bot difficulty and the turn prompt is more explicit, but it looks like a placeholder.

B fills the screen with a coherent dark/gold lobby, highlights the player's own seat, expands the rules inline and has a stronger CTA hierarchy; A leaves two-thirds of the phone blank and its pale pink selected states are low contrast. A is calmer and its collapsed accordion is arguably less busy.

A shows the whole table with rivers and the CHI toast in its own row without collisions; in B the CHI toast sits on top of the opponent rows and clips 'Bot (Standa'. A's centre river tiles are small and hard to read at phone size, while B's discard row is very legible.

B lifts the just-drawn tile out of the hand and highlights the wall draw spot on a rich 3D table, so what happened is obvious; A is a flat layout with four discards, a giant empty panel and a lone blue placeholder card in the middle. A's 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill is more explicit than B's small DRAW tag.

A's zoomed river makes every discard legible and the hand is large; B's PENG toast overlaps and clips the opponent labels. B counters with a clear claim bar (CHI / PASS) telling the player exactly what to do, whereas A's 'CHI Jin called' toast is ghosted and its header buttons overlap the wooden rim.

B's hero of 3D tiles and dice, gold primary CTA and dark theme make it feel like a game rather than a settings form, and it fills the viewport; A is clean but bland with half the screen empty. B's footer credit is clipped at the bottom edge and it is longer to scroll.

A has a designed empty state (fanned tiles, 'Nothing on the shelf yet', a Paste a replay action) and a LIBRARY eyebrow, so the screen feels finished; B is a header, a toggle and a blank cream page. B's larger typography is very readable.

B's angled 3D table with plum-backed walls, per-seat badges around the rim and a hand that spans the width is a proper desktop game view; A is a small flat green rectangle with tiny tiles and a big empty inner panel plus unused space below. A's LIVE/#SOLO chip and turn pill are informative.

A is the perspective table with readable tiles and clear seat badges; B is the flat 2D board with small tiles, an empty discard well, and a dead lower third of the viewport. B's centered 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill is a clearer prompt.

B uses a two-column layout that fits the whole lobby above the fold with strong gold selection states and a highlighted 'You' seat; A's pale pink selected states are hard to read and the page is a narrow column of beige cards. A does surface the match code copy chip and 'waiting for players' status, which B omits.

A keeps everything on the 3D table with the CHI/PASS claim bar floating near the river and no collisions; in B the PENG toast covers Mei's badge and the claim card sits off to the side of the board. B's discards and melds are easier to read individually, and its claim card is bigger.

B raises the drawn tile out of the hand and highlights the draw point on the wall, on a table with depth and lighting; A is the flat board with tiny river tiles and a mostly empty green well. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill is the one thing it does better.

A is a complete landing screen: hero tile fan, three balanced columns, a tutorial grid that fits, and drifting tile decorations; B's tutorial list runs off the bottom, the first two columns are mostly empty, and the pastel tile shapes look like unfinished placeholders. B's large 東 tile logo is a nice focal element.

B has a centred empty-state card with tile illustration, explanation and a Paste a replay action, plus a proper page header; A is a blank cream page with an oversized faint decorative shape that reads as a rendering artifact. A's full-width layout puts the header controls at the edges, which some might prefer.

B's perspective table with lit tile walls, wooden rim, dice plate and large readable hand tiles reads as a real game scene, while A is a flat green panel that is 70% empty 'DISCARDS' box with small tiles. Strongest point for A: everything fits in one compact layout with no dead band, and the player's name is not truncated (B shows 'Lucky Drag...').

A (the 3D table) has depth, a clear focal plate and big tiles; B is the same flat layout as pair 0 with a huge empty discard region and cramped 14-tile row. For B: the 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' chip is a slightly more explicit call to action than A's small 'DISCARD' pill.

B fills the phone screen with a coherent dark/gold glass design, highlights the player's own seat, and exposes the rules inline; A leaves the bottom half blank and its beige segmented controls have weak selected-state contrast. For A: it is lighter and arguably quicker to scan, with the Start button fixed to the bottom edge.

A shows the live river on a 3D table with the CHI toast cleanly placed under the seat strip; B's toast overlaps and clips the opponent list ('Bot (Standa'), and the giant lone draw tile floating in a sea of empty green looks unfinished. For B: its discard rows with owner colour bars are far more legible than A's tiny centre-table tiles.

B has a raised, selected tile in a large hand, a coherent 3D scene and no wasted space; A is mostly empty felt with one oversized pulsing tile. For A: the 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' banner and the discards row are clearer at a glance.

A's zoomed river makes every discard legible with real depth, and the close button is integrated into the chrome; B's toast collides with the opponent list and the layout is largely empty. Against A: the half-faded CHI toast sitting on the felt looks like a rendering artefact and the top-right wall is hard-clipped, so it is the less polished of the 3D shots.

B's dark hero with rendered tiles and dice, gold primary CTA and eyebrow label feels like a game landing page; A is a plain settings-style list. For A: it is compact, fully above the fold, and B's disabled 'Join match' button is a muddy brown and the floating background tiles add visual noise behind the form.

A has a proper empty state: illustrated tile fan, headline, guidance and a 'Paste a replay' action inside a card; B is a headline, a toggle and a bare paragraph over an empty beige page. For B: the light theme is calm and text contrast is fine, but that is all it offers.

B's tilted 3D table with wooden rim, dice plate and dealer chip is dramatically more attractive and uses the wide viewport; A is a flat board with a large empty inner rectangle and small tiles floating below it. For A: player badges sit directly beside each wall so ownership is instantly clear.
Same comparison as pair 8 in reverse: A's perspective table has depth and readable large tiles, B is the flat board with the empty discard rectangle. For B: it is compact and nothing is occluded.

B uses the desktop width for a two-column layout, highlights the user's seat in gold and has strong selected states on the skill toggles; A stacks everything in a narrow column with faint pink selection states. For A: it is very readable and its single-column order (seats, skill, rules, start) has a clear top-to-bottom flow.

A's 3D scene with the raised 一萬 tile and a compact floating CHI/PASS bar looks polished; B's PENG toast overlaps the top opponent badge and the right-hand claim panel floats off the table edge. For B: labelled melds ('PENG', 'CHI') and larger flat discards are easier to read than A's small centre-table tiles.

B's lifted tile and 3D table clearly signal 'your move' with real depth; A is mostly empty flat felt with a few scattered small discards. For A: the 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' chip and highlighted own badge are explicit.

A fits the whole menu including a 14-lesson tutorial grid into the viewport with a strong hero tile row and consistent dark/gold styling; B's tutorial column overflows the screen while the other two columns are largely empty. For B: the large 東 tile mark and cream palette are clean and friendly, and its buttons have stronger colour contrast.

B presents a designed empty state (tile fan illustration, headline, help text, 'Paste a replay') centred in a card; A is a header, a toggle and a sentence over a mostly blank page with a faint decorative background. For A: the light theme is easy on the eyes and nothing competes for attention.

B's rendered 3D table with wood rim, shaded walls, dice plate and large readable hand tiles reads as a real game; A is a flat green panel with a huge empty 'Discards' box and small tiles. A's one-row hand plus explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill is the only thing it does more clearly.

A (3D table, blue-back walls, depth, big hand tiles) is far more attractive and polished than B's flat felt with an empty discards area dominating the screen. B's compact single-row hand and clear turn label are its strongest points.

B's dark glass lobby with gold selected chips, a 'You · Online' seat highlight, subtitle copy and fully visible rules feels more premium and complete; A's cream version is tidy but leaves two-thirds of the screen empty and hides rules behind a collapsed row. A is quicker to scan and less busy.

A shows a convincing 3D table with melds, river and a legible CHI toast, and the drawn tile is clearly set apart; B's flat layout has a lone highlighted draw tile floating in a big empty area. B's discards row is more readable at a glance than A's small central river tiles.

B's 3D table with the freshly drawn tile raised in the hand and the wall break highlighted gives depth and clear 'what changed' cues; A is flat and mostly empty. A's turn pill and seat list are slightly more explicit about whose turn it is.

A's zoomed river with large legible discards and the wood rim looks more like a game and reads well; B is a plain list but has a very clear claim panel (tile, CHI, PASS). A's CHI toast is washed out over the felt and the top HUD pills overlap the rim, which cost it confidence.

B's dark hero with rendered tiles and dice, gold 'Play vs bots' CTA and title treatment feels like a game menu; A is a clean but generic cream card list. B's falling-tile decorations clutter the match-code input area and the footer is cut off, which are real polish nits in A's favour.

A has a designed empty state (fanned tile illustration, headline, helpful copy, 'Paste a replay' action) on a dark theme; B is a bare cream page with a paragraph and nothing else. B's higher-contrast toggle row is its only edge.

B's perspective 3D table with wood frame, shaded jade-plum walls, dealer chip and full-width hand looks like a modern game; A is a flat, small, centered 2D board with tiny tiles and lots of unused canvas. A's explicit 'YOUR TURN · DISCARD' pill next to the hand is more prominent than B's header pill.

A (3D perspective table, depth, large tiles, badges anchored to seats) is much more attractive and readable than B's small flat board floating in cream space. B's compact layout keeps everything in one glance, but at the cost of tiny tiles.

B's dark two-column lobby with gold selections and 'You · Online' seat state feels more polished and game-like; A is well balanced and centered but visually plain. A's centered composition uses the desktop width better than B's left-heavy layout with empty right and bottom areas.

A's 3D table with melds, river and a compact claim bar (tile, CHI, PASS) placed over the felt looks cohesive; B's flat layout has the PENG toast overlapping the Mei seat badge and a detached claim card off to the right. B's discards and melds are individually easier to read than A's small central tiles.

B's rendered table with the raised drawn tile, break-wall highlight and readable hand is more inviting; A's flat board with a few tiny discards in a big dark rectangle looks sparse. A's 'YOUR TURN · DRAW' pill beside the hand is a clearer call to action.

A's dark hero with a tile spread, three balanced cards and a compact 14-lesson tutorial grid fits the viewport and feels like a game landing page; B's light version has a tutorial list that runs off screen and tall cards with large empty areas. B's list gives lesson descriptions, which is helpful but hurts layout.

B provides a designed empty state with a tile illustration, headline, guidance and a 'Paste a replay' action on a dark theme; A is a nearly blank cream page with a faint decorative glyph. A's header controls are slightly larger and higher-contrast.
